findings.reason: yargs-parser.ts:978 now returns false whenever hasAllShortFlags(arg) is true, and hasAllShortFlags (945-966) checks each letter on its own, so '-ab' with a and b declared counts as known. Line 226 then doesn't push it as a positional, and the branch at 261-266 (taken when short-option-groups is false) sets key='ab', an undeclared option. Before the change, the guard skipped this check and hasFlagsMatching found 'ab' unknown.
findings.claim: Dropping the short-option-groups guard makes isUnknownOption treat '-ab' as known when groups are disabled, so with unknown-options-as-args it is parsed as option 'ab' instead of being kept in argv._.
findings.evidence: `isUnknownOption` now runs `if (hasAllShortFlags(arg)) { return false }` whatever the config. `hasAllShortFlags` checks each letter separately (`hasAnyFlag(letters[j])`), so `-ab` counts as known. With groups disabled, the parse loop then takes the branch at line 261 (`!configuration['short-option-groups'] && arg.match(/^-[^-]+/)`), sets `key = 'ab'`, and may run `setArg(key, next); i++`. That branch treats the whole word as one option name, not as separate letters. Before the change, the guard skipped the per-letter check when groups were off, and `hasFlagsMatching(normalFlag)` checked `ab` as one name, found it unknown, and `pushPositional(arg)` kept it.
